questions.explanation: When an individual pays the full cost with after-tax funds, disability benefits are generally not included in income. Employer-paid or pretax-funded coverage can produce different tax treatment.

questions.prompt: After paying covered medical expenses caused by a legally responsible third party, a health insurer asserts a permitted subrogation right. What is it seeking?
choices: Recovery from the responsible party to the extent of its applicable rights
An increase in the insured's life insurance face amount
A new beneficiary designation for the insured's retirement account
A guaranteed profit from the insured's unrelated investments
questions.explanation: Subrogation allows an insurer to pursue recovery associated with a loss it paid, subject to law and the contract. It is distinct from underwriting, premium collection, and a policy loan.

questions.prompt: A health applicant asks the producer to omit an ongoing treatment because it might delay underwriting. What should the producer do?
choices: Obtain truthful answers to the insurer's questions and submit the application accurately
Omit the treatment and ask the applicant to correct it only after a claim
Change the answer without the applicant's knowledge
Promise that a signed application can never affect a coverage decision
questions.explanation: A producer must not help falsify or conceal material application information. The insurer applies the product's lawful eligibility and underwriting rules to an accurate application.

questions.prompt: An insurer requests a valid authorization to obtain protected medical records for underwriting where permitted. What should the producer explain?
choices: The purpose and scope of the authorization and applicable privacy protections
That signing it publicly releases every medical record without restriction forever
That the producer may use the information for any unrelated purpose
That the applicant loses all rights to review the authorization
questions.explanation: Medical information must be handled under applicable privacy and authorization rules. The producer should explain the authorized purpose and avoid overstating either the right to disclose or the secrecy promised.

questions.prompt: An applicant asks whether an MIB record is itself an insurance company's final underwriting decision. Which response is accurate?
choices: It is an information resource that can prompt verification; the insurer makes its own underwriting decision
It is a consumer's credit score and nothing else
It gives the producer authority to issue any health policy immediately
questions.explanation: MIB information can help participating insurers identify and investigate inconsistencies. The insurer must evaluate applicable evidence and make the underwriting decision rather than treat a record as an automatic approval or denial.

questions.prompt: A health applicant gives the producer a premium check but no temporary coverage agreement applies. What should the producer avoid saying?
choices: That payment alone guarantees immediate unconditional coverage
That the insurer will review the application
That the effective date follows the contract and any valid receipt terms
That the applicant should keep a copy of any receipt
questions.explanation: Collecting a premium does not itself create unrestricted coverage. The effective date depends on the insurer's acceptance, any valid receipt or temporary agreement, and the applicable contract conditions.

questions.prompt: At delivery, a health policy includes a higher deductible than the applicant requested. What should the producer do?
choices: Explain the issued terms and obtain any required acceptance rather than describe the requested deductible as approved
Say the requested deductible controls despite the issued contract
Hide the schedule of benefits until after the first claim
Promise to personally rewrite the insurer's policy form
questions.explanation: Delivery includes explaining the actual coverage issued, including differences from the application. The applicant should be able to make an informed decision and complete any required acceptance process.

questions.prompt: An insured plans to replace an existing health policy with a new one. Which action best reduces the risk of an unintended coverage gap?
choices: Confirm the new policy's issuance, effective date, and relevant limitations before ending the old coverage
Cancel the old policy as soon as an application is requested
Assume that an initial quote guarantees immediate acceptance
Ignore the new policy's exclusions because the old plan covered the condition
questions.explanation: Replacement can change covered benefits, cost sharing, eligibility, and effective dates. Confirming the new contract before terminating the old one helps prevent gaps and unexpected limitations.

questions.prompt: Why is an insurance contract commonly described as unilateral?
choices: The insurer makes an enforceable promise to pay covered benefits in exchange for the applicant's consideration
Both parties must pay identical amounts after every claim
The applicant can require the insurer to cover every possible loss
The producer becomes personally liable for every covered benefit
questions.explanation: A unilateral insurance contract involves the insurer's promise to perform under the policy when conditions are satisfied. The owner can generally stop paying premiums, with contractual consequences such as lapse rather than a promise to keep paying forever.

questions.prompt: A small life insurance premium may lead to a large death benefit, while no claim may occur during a term. Which contract characteristic describes that unequal exchange depending on an uncertain event?
choices: Commutative with equal value exchanged in every case
A guaranteed savings deposit with no mortality risk
A partnership agreement dividing all insurer assets equally
questions.explanation: An aleatory contract makes performance depend on an uncertain event and can involve an unequal exchange of value. This is a standard characteristic of insurance contracts.

questions.prompt: Which Texas authority primarily regulates insurance companies and licensed insurance agents under state insurance law?
choices: The Texas Department of Insurance and Commissioner of Insurance
The county property appraisal district alone
The Federal Reserve as the issuer of every agent license
The Texas Real Estate Commission for all insurance products
questions.explanation: TDI and the Commissioner administer and enforce Texas insurance requirements within their statutory authority. Federal agencies and other state bodies have separate responsibilities and do not replace Texas insurance licensing oversight.

questions.prompt: What does an insurer's Texas certificate of authority generally establish?
choices: Authorization for the insurer to transact the specified insurance business in Texas
A personal producer license for every employee
A federal guarantee of the insurer's investment returns
An exemption from all Texas market-conduct rules
questions.explanation: A certificate of authority relates to an insurer's authority to transact insurance. Individual agent licensing and appointments are separate requirements, and authorization does not eliminate regulatory obligations.

questions.prompt: An insurance company is organized under Oklahoma law and is authorized to transact insurance in Texas. Relative to Texas, how is the company classified?
choices: Alien insurer solely because Oklahoma is another state
A mutual insurer solely because it operates across state lines
questions.explanation: An insurer organized in another U.S. state is foreign relative to Texas. A Texas-organized insurer is domestic, while an insurer organized under another country's laws is generally alien.

questions.prompt: Which ownership distinction between a stock insurer and a mutual insurer is generally correct?
choices: A stock insurer is owned by shareholders, while a mutual insurer is owned by its policyholder members
Every stock insurer is owned by the Texas government
Every mutual insurer is owned by its producers rather than its members
The words stock and mutual identify whether a company sells only health insurance
questions.explanation: Stock and mutual describe ownership structures rather than the lines of insurance sold. Shareholder ownership differs from mutual policyholder membership and does not by itself establish which coverage best fits a customer.

questions.prompt: A Texas resident passes the General Lines Life, Accident and Health exam but has not completed the licensing process. What should the applicant understand?
choices: Passing the exam alone does not authorize insurance sales; the required application, background-check process, and license approval still apply
The passing score automatically grants unrestricted authority to sell every insurance line
No application is needed once a premium is collected
A producer can use another person's license until approval arrives
questions.explanation: Exam passage is one licensing step and is not itself an issued license. Applicants must meet the applicable TDI requirements, and appointment and other authority requirements also apply before acting for an insurer.

questions.prompt: For a Texas General Lines Life, Accident, Health and HMO licensee subject to the ordinary continuing education requirement without an exemption, how many CE hours are required each two-year term?
questions.explanation: TDI requires 24 CE hours during each ordinary two-year term for this license, absent an applicable exemption or other special rule. Completing hours and paying any required fees or fines are separate compliance matters.

questions.prompt: For an ordinary Texas general lines renewal term expiring in 2026, which CE allocation meets the minimum ethics and classroom or classroom-equivalent requirements within the 24-hour total?
choices: At least 3 ethics hours and at least 12 classroom or classroom-equivalent hours
At least 2 ethics hours and no classroom-equivalent hours
At least 1 ethics hour and 24 self-study-only hours
No ethics hours if the agent sold only life policies
questions.explanation: TDI requires three ethics hours for current terms and at least half of the 24 hours in classroom or classroom-equivalent courses. The ethics hours are part of the total, and applicable exemptions or special requirements must be checked separately.

questions.prompt: A Texas insurance agent changes the business address and email used for licensing records. What should the agent do?
choices: Notify TDI immediately through the appropriate update process
Wait until the next claim is denied
Wait for the next two-year renewal without updating the records
Tell only one customer and assume TDI is informed
questions.explanation: TDI directs licensees to report contact information, legal name, and business name or address changes immediately. Keeping the licensing record current is the licensee's responsibility.

questions.prompt: A Texas producer presents a nonguaranteed life policy illustration as a guaranteed promise of future cash values. What is the primary market-conduct concern?
choices: Misrepresentation of policy benefits and guarantees
A proper explanation of guaranteed values
A required substitute for the policy summary
A valid way to avoid replacement disclosure
questions.explanation: Texas prohibits misleading statements about policy benefits, terms, and guarantees. Illustrated nonguaranteed values must not be represented as contractual guarantees.

questions.prompt: A Texas agent offers an applicant a private return of part of the commission as an inducement to buy life insurance, outside the policy and without an applicable legal exception. What prohibited practice is implicated?
choices: A properly declared participating policy dividend
questions.explanation: An off-contract financial inducement can constitute prohibited rebating under Texas law when no exception applies. It differs from benefits or dividends legitimately provided under the policy and governing rules.

questions.prompt: To discredit a competing insurer, a Texas agent knowingly circulates a false statement about its financial condition. Which prohibited practice is most directly involved?
choices: Permitted comparative advertising based on accurate facts
A required statement of insurable interest
questions.explanation: Knowingly circulating false or maliciously critical statements about an insurer's financial condition can constitute insurance defamation. Competition does not excuse deceptive statements.

questions.prompt: A Texas agent proposes to pay an unlicensed person a sales commission for soliciting and negotiating a life policy. No exception applies. What is the correct response?
choices: Do not pay a commission for insurance-agent services to a person who lacks the required license
Pay it if the unlicensed person calls the payment a consulting fee
Pay it whenever the applicant signs a waiver
Pay it if the commission is split into smaller payments
questions.explanation: Texas restricts commission payments for services requiring an insurance license. Renaming a commission or obtaining a customer's consent does not substitute for the required licensing authority.

questions.prompt: A Texas agent collects an applicant's initial premium for an insurer. Which handling of those funds is appropriate?
choices: Safeguard and account for the funds and remit them according to the authorized process
Use the premium for personal expenses until a claim is filed
Treat the premium as earned personal income immediately
Send the premium to an unrelated business without authorization
questions.explanation: Premium funds collected for an insurer must be handled according to fiduciary duties and applicable requirements. Personal use, conversion, or unauthorized handling can lead to serious licensing and legal consequences.

questions.prompt: A producer tells a prospect to buy a policy because the Texas Life and Health Insurance Guaranty Association guarantees every promised benefit without limits. What is wrong with that sales pitch?
choices: Association protections have eligibility and limits, and the association must not be used as a prohibited sales inducement
Every policy benefit and investment return is guaranteed without limits
Guaranty association membership replaces the need for an insurer's certificate of authority
Only agents who mention the association may sell life insurance
questions.explanation: Guaranty association protections are subject to statutory conditions and limits. They are not an unlimited guarantee and may not be used as a prohibited inducement to purchase insurance.

questions.prompt: Under the ordinary Texas life insurance grace-period requirement in Insurance Code Section 1101.005, what minimum period must a policy provide for a premium after the first payment?
choices: At least one month, during which the policy remains in force
Exactly three days with no coverage
No grace period after the first payment
An unlimited period without any premium obligation
questions.explanation: Section 1101.005 requires at least a one-month grace period for premiums after the first, with the policy remaining in force. The policy may provide for specified interest or deduction of an overdue premium from a death settlement, and special rules can require a longer period.

questions.prompt: A Texas life policy has remained in force during the insured's lifetime for two years from issue. Under the ordinary required incontestability provision, which exception is expressly retained?
choices: Any clerical error in an unrelated advertisement
Any decrease in the insurer's stock price
The beneficiary's move to another Texas county
questions.explanation: Texas Insurance Code Section 1101.006 requires incontestability after two years in force during the insured's lifetime, except for nonpayment of premiums. The statute also permits a specified wartime military-service condition; incontestability does not expand coverage beyond the contract.

questions.prompt: A Texas life application involves replacing an existing policy in a transaction subject to Chapter 1114. What should the producer do regarding the required replacement notice?
choices: Obtain the required signed notice, provide the applicant a copy, and submit required replacement information to the insurer
Avoid mentioning the existing coverage so the new insurer cannot identify replacement
Tell the applicant that replacement can never affect surrender charges or guarantees
Submit only the new premium and discard all replacement documents
questions.explanation: Texas replacement requirements seek informed comparison and accurate disclosure of existing coverage. Applicable agent duties include the required notice, signatures, copies, and information to the replacing insurer.

questions.prompt: A Texas annuity recommendation would pay the producer a higher commission but would not effectively address the consumer's stated needs. What should guide the recommendation?
choices: The consumer's best interest, supported by relevant information, required disclosures, and documentation
A promise that the state will reimburse any unsuitable purchase
The producer's sales quota without reviewing liquidity or surrender charges
questions.explanation: Texas requires agents to act in the consumer's best interest when recommending an annuity. Relevant financial needs, objectives, liquidity, costs, risks, conflicts, and the required disclosures and documentation must be considered.

questions.prompt: A replacement annuity transaction is subject to Texas Insurance Code Section 1114.053. What return period must the replacing insurer disclose after delivery?
choices: No return period is required for a replacement
questions.explanation: The replacing insurer must notify the owner of the right to return the policy or contract within 30 days of delivery. The statute specifies the refund, including a different valuation rule for variable or market value adjustment contracts.

questions.prompt: For an ordinary Texas life policy subject to Section 1101.011, excluding the private-placement separate-account exception, when must the policy provide for settlement after receipt of proof of death and the claimant's right to proceeds?
choices: Not later than two months after receipt of that proof
Only after the policy's original maturity date regardless of death
Not earlier than five years after receipt of proof
Whenever the producer chooses, with no contractual deadline
questions.explanation: Section 1101.011 requires settlement not later than two months after the insurer receives proof of death and the claimant's right to proceeds. The statute has a specific private-placement separate-account liquidity exception; other applicable claims requirements must also be followed.

questions.prompt: A Texas small employer health plan renewed on February 1, 2026 is subject to Section 1501.157 as amended by SB 896. To continue a covered employee's newborn coverage beyond the initial period, by when must the issuer receive notice of birth and any required additional premium?
choices: Not later than the 60th day after birth
Not later than the 31st day under the superseded deadline
Only at the next annual open enrollment regardless of birth date
questions.explanation: SB 896 extended the applicable notice and additional-premium deadline to the 60th day, with initial coverage ending on the 61st day if the requirements are not met. The amendment applies to plans delivered, issued for delivery, or renewed on or after January 1, 2026; earlier plans follow the prior law.

questions.prompt: Under the Texas small employer health insurance definition described by TDI, which employee-count range generally identifies a small employer, subject to applicable counting rules?
choices: Every employer regardless of employee count
questions.explanation: Texas insurance law generally defines a small employer as a business with two to 50 employees. Eligibility, employee-counting, participation, contribution, and other requirements still need to be evaluated for the particular plan.

questions.prompt: A Texas consumer receives a Medicare supplement policy and decides during the required free-look period that it is unsuitable. What return period does TDI describe for a refund?
choices: Only the day the application was signed
Five days after the first medical claim
One year after the policy lapses
questions.explanation: Texas Medicare supplement purchasers have a 30-day free-look opportunity to return the policy for a refund. This Medigap return right should not be confused with Medicare Advantage enrollment and disenrollment rules.

questions.prompt: A Texas long-term care insurance buyer receives the policy and wants time to review its terms. What minimum free-look period does TDI's long-term care guide describe?
choices: At least 30 days after receiving the policy
Seven days starting before the application is signed
No review period once any premium has been collected
questions.explanation: Texas long-term care buyers must receive at least 30 days to review the policy and return it for a refund under the free-look provision. Keeping evidence of receipt and timely return helps document exercise of that right.

questions.prompt: Where HIV-related testing is permitted in connection with a Texas insurance application, what must occur before the test under the applicable notice-and-consent requirement?
choices: The required notice must be given and written authorization obtained from the proposed insured or legally authorized person
The producer may order the test secretly without authorization
The applicant must waive every privacy right in all future medical care
The insurer may substitute an unrelated person's signature without legal authority
questions.explanation: Texas provides a specific Notice and Consent for HIV-Related Testing. The proposed insured or a legally authorized person must receive the required information and give the required written authorization; confidentiality and other governing rules also apply.

questions.prompt: A Texas consumer compares ACA-compliant individual major medical coverage with a limited accident policy. Which statement about essential health benefits is correct?
choices: ACA-compliant individual major medical coverage includes required categories such as mental health and substance use disorder services
A limited accident policy must provide every ACA essential health benefit because it is called insurance
Mental health services may always be excluded from every ACA-compliant individual plan
Essential health benefits consist only of accidental death benefits
questions.explanation: ACA-compliant individual and small-group major medical plans cover essential health benefit categories, including mental health and substance use disorder services. Limited benefit products are not equivalent substitutes, and cost sharing and other lawful plan terms still apply.

questions.prompt: A Texas resident wants to compare Marketplace health plans and apply for any available financial assistance for which the household qualifies. Which website is the federal Marketplace used in Texas?
choices: Medicare.gov as the Marketplace for every adult under 65
The Texas Real Estate Commission website
questions.explanation: Texas uses the federal Health Insurance Marketplace at HealthCare.gov. Eligibility, enrollment periods, plan choices, and financial assistance depend on the household's circumstances and current requirements.

questions.prompt: A Texas HMO enrollee wants the document describing benefits, limitations, obtaining care, and complaint and appeal procedures. Which document should the agent identify?
questions.explanation: An HMO evidence of coverage explains how the plan operates, including covered services, limitations, obtaining care, and complaint and appeal rights. A marketing summary alone is not a substitute for understanding the coverage document.

questions.prompt: A Texas HMO enrollee has a genuine medical emergency while away from home and goes to the nearest out-of-network emergency facility. Which statement is correct?
choices: Emergency coverage cannot be denied solely because the emergency provider is outside the HMO network
All out-of-network emergency care is automatically excluded
The enrollee must return home before seeking emergency evaluation
The HMO may require a routine primary care referral before emergency stabilization
questions.explanation: Texas HMO requirements include emergency care access, including qualifying out-of-network emergency services. Applicable cost sharing, emergency-care standards, and billing protections must be considered rather than applying ordinary routine-care network restrictions.

questions.prompt: A Texas HMO's network cannot provide a medically necessary covered specialist service. What should the enrollee and agent do?
choices: Use the plan's process to arrange access to the covered service outside the network when required
Assume the service becomes permanently excluded because the network lacks a specialist
Describe every elective out-of-network service as automatically covered without coordination
Cancel the plan before asking about access or appeal rights
questions.explanation: An HMO's network responsibilities include access to covered medically necessary care. When the network cannot provide the service, applicable referral and out-of-network arrangements should be pursued under the plan and Texas requirements.

questions.prompt: A laptop touchpad stops responding immediately after the user presses a function-key combination. An external mouse still works. What should the technician check first?
choices: Whether the touchpad was disabled with its keyboard shortcut
Whether the laptop battery needs replacement
Whether the SSD has reached its write limit
Whether the wireless access point is overloaded
questions.explanation: Many laptops provide a function-key shortcut that disables the touchpad. Checking that setting addresses the immediate change before replacing hardware or drivers.

questions.prompt: A laptop battery is visibly swollen and pushing against the case. What is the safest response?
choices: Stop using the laptop, disconnect external power safely, and arrange approved battery replacement
Press the battery flat before closing the case
Puncture the battery to release trapped gas
Continue charging until a diagnostic completes
questions.explanation: A swollen lithium-ion battery is a safety hazard. Stop using and charging the device and follow the manufacturer's handling and disposal procedures; do not crush or puncture it.

questions.prompt: A workstation receives 169.254.18.42/16 and cannot reach resources outside its local link. Which service should the technician investigate first?
questions.explanation: An IPv4 link-local address commonly indicates that the client could not obtain a DHCP lease. DNS does not assign the client's IP configuration.

questions.prompt: A user can reach a web server by its IP address but cannot resolve its hostname. Which service is the most likely source of the problem?
questions.explanation: Successful IP connectivity with failed name resolution points to DNS. Check the configured DNS server and the relevant records before changing working physical connections.

questions.prompt: Which device forwards packets between different IP networks using a routing table?
questions.explanation: A router selects a next hop for traffic between IP networks. A basic Layer 2 switch forwards Ethernet frames within a local network using MAC addresses.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to verify which physical cable connects a wall jack to a patch-panel port. Which tool combination is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: A tone generator places an identifiable signal on a cable and a probe locates that signal at the other end. This identifies the cable without relying on its label.

questions.prompt: A desktop must use a nearby wired Ethernet network but has no built-in Ethernet port. Which accessory is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: A USB-to-Ethernet adapter adds a wired network interface when its connector, driver, and operating system are compatible. The other accessories do not provide Ethernet connectivity.

questions.prompt: A customer wants one cable to a laptop dock for power, an external display, and USB peripherals. What must be checked before selecting the dock?
choices: The laptop port and dock support the required video mode and USB Power Delivery capacity
Every USB-C port automatically supports all docking features
The dock has a VGA connector even if no VGA display is used
The laptop has an optical drive
questions.explanation: USB-C describes a connector, not a guarantee of video output, data speed, or charging capability. Match the host's supported features and the dock's power budget to the workload.

questions.prompt: A desktop with four memory slots has two identical DIMMs. What is the best way to choose their slots for dual-channel operation?
choices: Follow the motherboard manual's recommended two-DIMM channel configuration
Install both DIMMs into whichever adjacent slots are closest
Mix one DDR4 DIMM with one DDR5 DIMM
Use only one DIMM because dual-channel requires four
questions.explanation: Motherboard slot assignments vary, so the manual identifies the correct paired slots. Compatible modules in the recommended channels allow the memory controller to use dual-channel operation.

questions.prompt: A technician is replacing an M.2 storage device. What must be confirmed in addition to the module's physical length?
choices: The slot and drive support the same storage interface, such as SATA or PCIe NVMe
All M.2 devices use the same electrical interface
The drive has a separate Molex power connector
The drive uses an external USB cable
questions.explanation: M.2 is a form factor and connector family. A physically suitable module still needs a compatible SATA or PCIe/NVMe interface and platform support.

questions.prompt: A workstation needs to continue operating after either one of two identical storage drives fails. Which RAID level meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: RAID 1 mirrors data across drives and can tolerate one member's failure in a two-drive mirror. Mirroring does not replace backups against deletion, corruption, or ransomware.

questions.prompt: A desktop frequently overheats under load after being moved to a dusty office. What is the best initial hardware maintenance action after safely powering it down?
choices: Inspect and clear blocked vents, heatsinks, and fans using approved methods
questions.explanation: Restricted airflow and dust accumulation can cause overheating. Restore cooling and verify fan operation before considering component replacement or performance changes.

questions.prompt: A computer powers on but repeatedly emits a beep pattern and shows no video after a RAM upgrade. What should the technician do next?
choices: Consult the system's POST-code documentation and verify the RAM is compatible and seated
questions.explanation: POST beeps can identify hardware initialization failures. The timing after a memory change makes module seating and compatibility relevant, but the manufacturer's code documentation should guide diagnosis.

questions.prompt: A desktop clock resets whenever mains power is disconnected, and firmware settings return to defaults. Which component is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: The motherboard battery maintains the real-time clock and retained firmware settings when external power is absent. A weak battery can cause lost time and reset configuration.

questions.prompt: A laser printer produces pages on which toner rubs off easily. Which assembly should be investigated first?
questions.explanation: The fuser bonds toner to paper using heat and pressure. Loose toner after printing suggests a fusing problem rather than a network or document-feeding fault.

questions.prompt: A laser printer prints a repeating vertical streak on every page, including an internal test page. What does the internal test establish?
choices: The fault is within the printer rather than only the workstation's application or print driver
The network switch must be replaced
The user's account has no print permission
questions.explanation: An internal test bypasses the workstation and its driver. A repeated defect there points to the printer's imaging, toner, or paper path and should be investigated using its maintenance guidance.

questions.prompt: An inkjet printer has missing lines in its output after weeks without use. Which maintenance step is most appropriate first?
choices: Run the manufacturer's nozzle-check and printhead-cleaning routine
Change the network's DHCP lease duration
Add toner to the ink cartridge
questions.explanation: Dried ink or blocked nozzles can cause gaps in inkjet output. Use the supported cleaning routine before replacing components; inkjet printers do not use toner or a laser fuser.

questions.prompt: A wireless client has poor performance only when it is far from the access point behind several concrete walls. What is the most likely contributing factor?
questions.explanation: Distance and dense building materials reduce received wireless signal strength. Improve access-point placement or coverage after checking the actual signal and interference conditions.

questions.prompt: A small office is experiencing interference from many nearby 2.4 GHz wireless networks. What is a reasonable improvement for compatible nearby clients?
choices: Move them to a properly planned 5 GHz or 6 GHz wireless network
Set all access points to the same 2.4 GHz channel
Increase the DHCP address lease to one year
questions.explanation: Using another supported band can reduce competition in the crowded 2.4 GHz spectrum. Coverage, client compatibility, channel planning, and local regulatory requirements still matter.

questions.prompt: A workstation must use TCP port 443 to reach a secure public website. Which application protocol normally uses that destination port?
questions.explanation: HTTPS normally uses TCP 443 for HTTP protected with TLS. SSH commonly uses 22, SMTP 25, and RDP 3389, so those ports do not match this request.

questions.prompt: A server delivers shared network storage as files and folders over SMB. Which storage category best describes it?
questions.explanation: A NAS makes file-based storage available across a network. Direct-attached storage connects locally to a host rather than exposing network file shares itself.

questions.prompt: A team wants separate guest operating systems running on one physical host. Which component manages the virtual machines' access to hardware?
questions.explanation: A hypervisor creates and manages virtual machines and allocates their CPU, memory, and other resources. Each guest can run its own operating system within the virtualized environment.

questions.prompt: A browser-based service provides ready-to-use email without the customer managing mail-server software or the underlying servers. Which cloud service model fits?
questions.explanation: SaaS provides a complete application managed by the provider. With IaaS, customers typically manage guest operating systems and their installed applications.

questions.prompt: A host cannot start a virtual machine because the VM configuration requests more RAM than the host can allocate. What should be evaluated first?
choices: The VM memory allocation and the host's available RAM
questions.explanation: Virtual machines consume host memory as well as CPU and storage resources. Adjust allocations or capacity based on the workload and the host's available resources.

questions.prompt: A smartphone can browse over cellular data but cannot join any Wi-Fi network after airplane mode was enabled. What should be checked first?
choices: Whether Wi-Fi is currently enabled in the device settings
Whether the cellular data plan has roaming
Whether the laptop's RAM is dual-channel
Whether the public DNS zone has a new MX record
questions.explanation: Airplane mode can disable radios, and users may re-enable them individually. Verify the device's Wi-Fi state before replacing networking hardware or changing unrelated services.

questions.prompt: A mobile device needs centralized enforcement of a screen lock and the ability to remove company data if lost. Which solution is appropriate?
questions.explanation: MDM supports centralized device policies and supported remote-management actions. Enrollment mode and platform capabilities determine whether an organization can wipe company data or the entire device.

questions.prompt: A user reports that a monitor displays 'No signal' after the computer was moved. Which check should come first?
choices: Verify the display cable connections and selected input source
questions.explanation: Loose cables or an incorrect input selection are simple, common causes after moving equipment. Confirm the display path before disruptive repairs.

questions.prompt: A desktop loses network connectivity when its damaged patch cable is flexed. Which troubleshooting action best tests the suspected cause?
choices: Replace it temporarily with a known-good compatible cable
Create a new local user account
questions.explanation: A known-good cable isolates a suspected physical-layer fault. Once connectivity is stable, document the finding and replace the damaged cable permanently.

questions.prompt: A technician has identified a likely cause and developed a repair plan. Before applying a change that could interrupt a shared service, what should happen?
choices: Assess the impact and obtain the required change authorization
Apply it immediately without notifying affected users
Disable backups to reduce troubleshooting noise
questions.explanation: Troubleshooting plans should account for service impact, safeguards, and the organization's change procedure. Required authorization helps avoid an unplanned interruption to other users.

questions.prompt: After replacing a failed workstation network adapter, what completes the troubleshooting process?
choices: Verify full functionality, apply relevant preventive measures, and document the work
Close the ticket as soon as the adapter is installed
Delete the previous network configuration records
Ask the user to test it next month
questions.explanation: A component replacement alone does not prove resolution. Confirm the reported issue is resolved, check related functionality, and record the cause and corrective action.

questions.prompt: A Windows workstation becomes unstable immediately after a display-driver update. Which recovery action most directly reverses that change?
choices: Roll back the driver using Device Manager if a previous driver is available
questions.explanation: Driver rollback restores the prior driver when Windows has retained it. This targets the recent change with less disruption than reinstalling the operating system.

questions.prompt: A Windows application is unresponsive while the rest of the desktop works. Which tool is most appropriate to end that application's process?
questions.explanation: Task Manager shows running processes and can end an unresponsive application. Warn the user that unsaved work in that application may be lost.

questions.prompt: A Windows technician needs detailed application and system event logs for a recurring crash. Which tool should be used?
questions.explanation: Event Viewer exposes Windows event logs that can help correlate failures with services, drivers, or applications. Logs support diagnosis rather than proving a cause without further investigation.

questions.prompt: Which Windows command displays the workstation's IPv4 address, subnet mask, and default gateway?
questions.explanation: ipconfig reports network interface configuration. Its output helps establish addressing and gateway settings before investigating routing or DNS failures.

questions.prompt: A technician suspects Windows protected system files were damaged. Which command checks their integrity and attempts repair from available sources?
questions.explanation: System File Checker checks protected Windows system files and can repair detected corruption. If it cannot repair them, further servicing or recovery may be required.

questions.prompt: An NTFS file has a read permission entry for a group and an applicable explicit deny-write entry for that same group. What happens when an ordinary member attempts to modify the file?
choices: Read permission automatically grants write permission
questions.explanation: An applicable deny entry can prevent the requested write access. Reading and modifying are separate permissions, so a read grant alone does not authorize editing.

questions.prompt: A Windows device stores sensitive customer records and could be stolen. Which control best protects the data on its internal drive while the device is powered off?
choices: BitLocker drive encryption with properly managed recovery information
questions.explanation: Full-volume encryption protects stored data if an attacker removes the drive or boots another operating system. Recovery keys must be stored securely so authorized users can recover access.

questions.prompt: A standard user receives a User Account Control prompt when installing approved system software. What is the intended purpose of the prompt?
choices: Require appropriate elevation before a change needing administrator privileges
Encrypt every file uploaded by the application
Guarantee that the installer is malware-free
Turn off audit logging for the installation
questions.explanation: UAC separates ordinary user activity from elevated operations. Approval or administrator credentials authorize elevation but do not establish that the software is trustworthy.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to list hidden files in a Linux directory. Which command is appropriate?
questions.explanation: The -a option includes hidden entries whose names begin with a dot. pwd prints the current directory, while cd and mkdir change or create directories.

questions.prompt: A Linux file should be readable and writable by its owner, with no access for the group or others. Which permission mode fits?
questions.explanation: Mode 600 grants read and write to the owner and no permissions to other classes. The other modes allow additional users to read, execute, or modify the file.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to inspect the last lines of a Linux text log as new records are added. Which command is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: tail -f follows a file and displays newly appended lines. Changing permissions or removing the log would disrupt observation rather than display events.

questions.prompt: A macOS user wants automated, versioned backups to a supported backup destination. Which built-in feature is designed for this purpose?
questions.explanation: Time Machine maintains backups that can support restoring files or a system. Verify the destination and successful backups instead of assuming the feature is working merely because it is enabled.

questions.prompt: A company plans an operating-system upgrade on a workstation with a specialized business application. What should happen before the upgrade?
choices: Verify hardware and application compatibility and create a recoverable backup
Upgrade first and ask about compatibility afterward
questions.explanation: Compatibility checks reduce the risk of losing essential functionality. A verified backup and recovery plan provide a way to recover if the upgrade fails.

questions.prompt: A workstation boots correctly in Safe Mode but fails during a normal startup. What does this observation suggest?
choices: An additional driver, service, or startup application may be involved
The monitor has no electrical power
All hardware is proven to be fault-free
The system drive is definitely empty
questions.explanation: Safe Mode loads a reduced set of drivers and services. Successful startup there narrows investigation but does not prove every hardware component is healthy.

questions.prompt: A user receives a message demanding an immediate password reset through an unfamiliar link. What is the best response?
choices: Report it and verify the request through a known trusted channel
Enter credentials quickly to avoid account suspension
Forward it to coworkers asking them to sign in
questions.explanation: Urgency and an unfamiliar sign-in link are phishing indicators. A separately verified channel avoids trusting contact details controlled by the sender.

questions.prompt: A user gives a remote caller a one-time authentication code, believing the caller is IT support. Which attack technique is illustrated?
questions.explanation: The attacker manipulates the user into revealing an authentication secret. One-time codes should only be entered into a trusted sign-in flow initiated by the user.

questions.prompt: A technician suspects an actively spreading malware infection on a workstation. What is the best immediate containment action under the incident procedure?
choices: Isolate the workstation from the network while preserving evidence
Copy suspicious files to shared drives for colleagues to open
Use the infected workstation for administrator password resets
questions.explanation: Network isolation can limit spread and remote control. Follow the incident plan and preserve relevant evidence instead of conducting sensitive activity on the suspected system.

questions.prompt: Why should a user have a standard account for routine work and a separate privileged account for administration?
choices: It limits the privileges available to everyday applications and mistakes
It guarantees phishing messages cannot arrive
It removes the need for software updates
It makes every file publicly readable
questions.explanation: Least privilege reduces the impact of compromised applications and accidental changes. Administrative access should be used only when the task requires it.

questions.prompt: A shared workstation must lock automatically when unattended. Which setting most directly implements this requirement?
choices: Require authentication after a short inactivity lock timeout
Turn off the monitor without locking the session
Keep a shared administrator session open
questions.explanation: An authenticated inactivity lock prevents someone from using an unattended logged-in session. A dark display alone does not provide an access control.

questions.prompt: A laptop is leaving the company permanently and contains confidential data on an SSD. What should the technician do before disposal?
choices: Use an approved sanitization method suitable for the SSD and verify the result
Move the files to the recycle bin without emptying it
questions.explanation: Ordinary deletion does not ensure data is unrecoverable. Use an approved sanitization, cryptographic erase, or destruction process appropriate to the device and data classification.

questions.prompt: A technician is asked to examine suspected illegal material on a company device. What is the correct approach?
choices: Follow the organization's reporting and evidence-preservation procedure
Copy it to a personal account for later study
Delete it to protect the employee
Discuss it openly with unrelated coworkers
questions.explanation: Evidence handling must follow policy and applicable authority. Avoid unnecessary access, copying, alteration, or disclosure that could damage evidence or privacy.

questions.prompt: A department needs to restore a file accidentally overwritten yesterday. Which capability is most directly useful?
choices: A tested backup retaining previous file versions
questions.explanation: Versioned backups can recover an earlier state after an accidental overwrite. RAID and faster connectivity do not preserve old content on their own.

questions.prompt: After a full backup on Sunday, an incremental backup is made each evening. Which backups are generally needed to restore to Wednesday evening?
choices: Sunday's full backup and the Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday incremental backups
Monday's incremental backup and no full backup
questions.explanation: A typical incremental chain records changes since the previous backup. Restoration needs the full backup and each required incremental in sequence.

questions.prompt: A company has approved a workstation configuration change. What should the technician document before implementation to support recovery?
choices: The current configuration, planned steps, and rollback procedure
An instruction to discard all backups
questions.explanation: A documented baseline and rollback plan help reverse an unsuccessful change. Records should also identify validation steps and the authorized change window.

questions.prompt: A user asks a technician to install software using the technician's personal license. What should happen?
choices: Check the organization's approved software and licensing process
Install it because any paid license permits unlimited business use
Share the technician's personal account credentials
questions.explanation: Software use must follow its license terms and the organization's approval process. Personal ownership does not establish that installation on a company device is authorized.

questions.prompt: A workstation must connect to a remote corporate network over an untrusted Internet connection. Which solution provides an encrypted tunnel?
questions.explanation: A VPN protects supported traffic between the device and the VPN endpoint. Its configuration and routing determine which traffic is included in the tunnel.

questions.prompt: A user reports that a known printer fails only after changing the default paper size in an application. What should be checked first?
choices: The application's print settings and their agreement with the printer's supported paper configuration
questions.explanation: The issue follows an application-level print-setting change. Verify that configuration and reproduce the problem before replacing working printer hardware.

questions.prompt: A technician handles a support call with a frustrated customer. Which response is most professional?
choices: Listen, confirm the problem and business impact, and explain the next steps clearly
Interrupt repeatedly to finish the call faster
questions.explanation: Clear listening and expectation setting support effective troubleshooting. Keep communication respectful and disclose only information relevant and authorized for the call.

questions.prompt: A power supply inside a desktop is suspected to have failed. Which action is safest for a general support technician?
choices: Replace the complete approved unit after safely disconnecting power
Open the power supply and touch its internal capacitors
Work on its internal board while it is plugged in
questions.explanation: Power supplies can retain hazardous charge after being unplugged. General desktop support should replace the approved assembly rather than open or bypass its safety components.

questions.prompt: A support technician resolves a startup failure by removing a defective peripheral. What should be included when closing the incident?
choices: The symptoms, tests, identified cause, corrective action, and verified outcome
A recommendation to stop keeping incident records
questions.explanation: Useful incident documentation explains what failed and how resolution was verified. It supports future troubleshooting while avoiding unnecessary sensitive data.

questions.prompt: A retailer wants to add computing capacity during short seasonal sales and remove it afterward. Which cloud characteristic best supports this goal?
questions.explanation: Elasticity allows capacity to grow and shrink with demand. It reduces the need to own enough hardware for a brief peak throughout the year.

questions.prompt: A company moves from buying servers in advance to paying for consumed cloud resources. Which financial change does this illustrate?
choices: Trading substantial upfront infrastructure expense for variable usage expense
Requiring the same server purchase before every deployment
questions.explanation: Cloud consumption can replace large upfront infrastructure purchases with variable costs. Organizations still need cost management because consumption and related services remain billable.

questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes an AWS Availability Zone from an AWS Region?
choices: A Region is a geographic area containing multiple Availability Zones
An Availability Zone contains all AWS Regions
Every Region consists of exactly one physical server
An Availability Zone is a customer billing account
questions.explanation: A Region contains multiple isolated Availability Zones connected by low-latency networking. Deploying across zones can reduce the impact of a zone-level failure.

questions.prompt: An application must remain available if one Availability Zone fails. Which design best addresses that requirement?
choices: Deploy application instances across multiple Availability Zones
Place every instance on one host in one zone
Store the only backup on the same instance
Use a longer administrator password as the sole availability measure
questions.explanation: Using multiple zones reduces dependence on a single zone's facilities. The application must also handle traffic routing and data availability across those zones.

questions.prompt: Which customer action remains a responsibility when running an application on Amazon EC2?
choices: Replacing failed physical server disks in an AWS data centre
Maintaining the physical power systems in the AWS facility
Controlling physical access to AWS server racks
questions.explanation: For EC2, AWS manages the physical infrastructure while customers manage the guest operating system and their applications. Responsibility boundaries change with the managed service used.

questions.prompt: An organization uses Amazon RDS rather than installing a database on EC2. Which responsibility generally remains with the customer?
choices: Managing application data and database access permissions
Replacing the database host's physical memory
Maintaining the data centre's cooling equipment
Repairing the underlying hardware network cards
questions.explanation: RDS manages many infrastructure and database administration tasks, but customers still control their data and access configuration. A managed service does not remove all customer security responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Which practice best protects the AWS account root user?
choices: Enable multifactor authentication and reserve root use for tasks that require it
Create root access keys for every developer
Use root credentials for routine application calls
Share the root password with the support queue
questions.explanation: The root identity has extensive privileges. Protect it with MFA and use appropriately scoped identities for routine administration and workloads.

questions.prompt: An application on EC2 needs temporary permissions to read one S3 bucket. Which approach is preferred?
choices: Attach an IAM role with the necessary permissions to the instance
Embed the root user's access keys in application code
Give all developers the same permanent administrator keys
questions.explanation: An instance role supplies temporary credentials that AWS rotates. A scoped policy limits the application to the access it needs without embedding long-lived secrets.

questions.prompt: A company wants workforce users to access several AWS accounts through centrally managed sign-in. Which service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: IAM Identity Center supports centralized workforce access to AWS accounts and supported applications. It addresses user access rather than DNS or block storage.

questions.prompt: Which policy design follows least privilege for an application that only reads objects from a specific S3 location?
choices: Allow only the required read actions on the required resources
Allow every action on every AWS resource
Grant account administrator access to simplify deployment
Publish the application's credentials so users can troubleshoot
questions.explanation: Least privilege limits actions and resources to the task. Broad administrator policies create unnecessary access even if the application currently performs only reads.

questions.prompt: An auditor asks which principal changed a security group and when. Which AWS service provides the relevant account activity records?
questions.explanation: CloudTrail records supported AWS account and API activity, including identity and timing details. It is used for auditing actions rather than caching application content.

questions.prompt: An operations team wants an alarm when an EC2 instance's CPU utilization remains high. Which service is the best fit?
questions.explanation: CloudWatch collects operational metrics and can trigger alarms. CloudTrail focuses on account activity, while Artifact provides access to compliance reports and agreements.

questions.prompt: An auditor needs AWS compliance reports supplied by AWS. Which service provides access to them?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact provides supported compliance reports and agreements. Customers still evaluate whether their own workload configuration and processes meet their obligations.

questions.prompt: A security team wants managed detection of suspicious activity based on supported AWS telemetry. Which service best fits?
questions.explanation: GuardDuty analyzes supported data sources for threats and suspicious behavior. It produces security findings and does not replace permissions management or incident response.

questions.prompt: A company needs managed keys for encrypting data in supported AWS services. Which service is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: AWS KMS supports creating and controlling cryptographic keys used by supported services and applications. Key permissions and configuration remain important customer responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Which AWS service provides resizable virtual servers that let a customer manage the guest operating system?
questions.explanation: EC2 provides virtual compute instances. Customers choose an image and instance resources and manage the guest operating system, unlike object storage or DNS services.

questions.prompt: A team wants to run a function in response to uploaded objects without provisioning servers. Which compute service fits?
questions.explanation: Lambda runs event-driven functions without the customer managing servers. The team still manages its function code, permissions, and supported runtime configuration.

questions.prompt: Which service is best suited to storing image files as objects accessed through APIs?
questions.explanation: S3 stores objects within buckets and exposes APIs for access. It is different from block storage attached to a virtual machine or a relational database.

questions.prompt: An EC2 instance needs a persistent block device for its operating system. Which service is appropriate?
questions.explanation: EBS provides block storage volumes for EC2. A volume's attachment and availability characteristics must be considered when designing recovery and zone-level resilience.

questions.prompt: Several Linux instances need concurrent access to a managed shared file system. Which service is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: EFS supplies a shared file system that supported clients can mount. Archival object storage is not a drop-in shared filesystem for active applications.

questions.prompt: A team wants a managed relational database that supports SQL without managing the underlying database host. Which service is appropriate?
questions.explanation: RDS manages supported relational database engines and infrastructure tasks. The customer still designs the schema, controls access, and manages application use of the database.

questions.prompt: A workload needs a managed key-value database with flexible scaling and no database servers to administer. Which service best fits?
questions.explanation: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value and document database. It does not require the customer to install a database engine on EC2 instances.

questions.prompt: A web application needs to distribute incoming requests among healthy targets. Which service provides this capability?
questions.explanation: Elastic Load Balancing distributes traffic to configured healthy targets. It is commonly paired with multiple instances and zones to support resilient applications.

questions.prompt: A company wants its group of EC2 instances to increase or decrease automatically with workload demand. Which service provides this function?
questions.explanation: EC2 Auto Scaling adjusts the number of instances in a group using configured policies and health information. Load balancing routes requests but does not itself create the required instance capacity.

questions.prompt: A website wants to cache content close to users around the world. Which service is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: CloudFront is a content delivery network using edge locations. Caching content near users can reduce latency and reduce requests to the origin.

questions.prompt: A company needs managed DNS hosting and domain-based traffic routing. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Route 53 provides DNS and supported routing capabilities. DNS maps names and routing policies to endpoints; it is separate from block storage and job execution.

questions.prompt: An application should place work in a queue so workers can process it independently of the request service. Which service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: SQS provides managed message queues that decouple producers and consumers. Workers must still handle delivery semantics and make processing appropriately idempotent.

questions.prompt: A finance team wants a notification when monthly AWS cost reaches a configured threshold. Which service is the best fit?
questions.explanation: AWS Budgets can monitor supported cost or usage targets and send threshold alerts. An alert alone does not guarantee that spending immediately stops.

questions.prompt: A team wants to explore historical AWS spending by service and time period. Which tool is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Cost Explorer visualizes and analyzes cost and usage data. Budgets focuses on targets and notifications, while permissions simulation serves a different purpose.

questions.prompt: A batch job can tolerate interruption and resume later. Which EC2 purchasing option may reduce cost by using spare capacity?
choices: Dedicated Hosts as a mandatory choice
Only On-Demand Instances regardless of interruption tolerance
A physical server purchased from AWS
questions.explanation: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity and can be interrupted. A suitable workload must tolerate interruptions and preserve progress or retry work safely.

questions.prompt: An organization restricts access to payroll records so only authorized staff can read them. Which security objective is addressed most directly?
questions.explanation: Confidentiality protects information from unauthorized disclosure. Integrity addresses unauthorized alteration, while availability concerns timely access to systems and data.

questions.prompt: A recipient verifies a downloaded file's hash against a trusted published hash. Which property is being checked most directly?
questions.explanation: Matching a trusted hash helps detect a changed file. The trusted source for the expected hash matters because a hash supplied by an attacker does not establish authenticity.

questions.prompt: A digital signature on a document can help a recipient establish which combination of properties?
questions.explanation: A digital signature can demonstrate that signed data has not changed and that the signer controlled the corresponding private key. It does not encrypt the document's contents by itself.

questions.prompt: A security camera records entries into a restricted server room. Which control function is its recording primarily providing?
questions.explanation: Recorded surveillance helps detect and investigate events. A visible camera can also deter behavior, but the recording function provides evidence rather than repairing damage.

questions.prompt: A company cannot install a required patch immediately and temporarily isolates the affected system behind stricter access controls. How is the temporary alternative best described?
questions.explanation: A compensating control provides an alternative safeguard when the preferred control cannot currently be applied. Its effectiveness and residual risk still need evaluation.

questions.prompt: An employee receives a convincing text message asking them to sign in through a link controlled by an attacker. What is this attack called?
questions.explanation: Smishing is phishing through text messages. Vishing uses voice communication, while tailgating concerns physical entry behind an authorized person.

questions.prompt: A user receives repeated unexpected MFA approval prompts after an attacker obtains the user's password. What is the most appropriate response?
choices: Deny the prompts, report the activity, and secure the compromised account
Approve one prompt to stop the notifications
Tell the caller the next one-time code
Disable logging until the prompts stop
questions.explanation: Repeated prompts may be an MFA fatigue attack. Do not approve unknown requests; report them and follow the account recovery and incident procedures.

questions.prompt: A web application builds SQL by concatenating untrusted input. Which mitigation most directly addresses SQL injection?
choices: Use parameterized queries with appropriate input handling
Hide the database server's hostname in a comment
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries separate data from executable SQL syntax. Validation and least-privileged database access add protection but do not justify unsafe query construction.

questions.prompt: An attacker places JavaScript in a comment that later executes in other users' browsers. Which vulnerability is demonstrated?
choices: A buffer underrun in a printer
questions.explanation: Stored XSS occurs when malicious content is saved and later rendered as executable browser code. Context-aware output encoding and safe rendering prevent untrusted text from becoming active content.

questions.prompt: An application allows a signed-in user to download another user's invoice by changing an invoice ID in the URL. Which missing control is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Authentication alone does not authorize access to every object. The server must verify that the current principal can access the particular invoice on each request.

questions.prompt: A network is divided so a compromise of a guest Wi-Fi client does not directly expose payroll servers. Which technique supports this design?
choices: Network segmentation with enforced access rules
Putting every host into the same broadcast domain
questions.explanation: Segmentation limits communication between areas with different trust requirements. Enforcement rules are necessary; merely naming separate groups does not restrict traffic.

questions.prompt: Which statement best reflects a zero trust approach?
choices: Evaluate access explicitly using identity, context, and policy rather than trusting network location alone
Trust every request originating from the office network
Grant all permissions after the first successful login
questions.explanation: Zero trust does not treat network presence as sufficient proof of trust. Access decisions should be limited to the resource and conditions needed for the request.

questions.prompt: A user authenticates with a password and a hardware security key. Which description is correct?
choices: Two different authentication factor categories are used
A username supplies a third secret factor
Two passwords always provide the same factor diversity
questions.explanation: The password is something the user knows and the key is something the user has. Distinct factor categories provide stronger protection than two secrets from the same category.

questions.prompt: A service account needs database read access for one application and no interactive login. Which configuration best follows least privilege?
choices: Grant only necessary read permissions and restrict its allowed use
Add it to every administrative group
Let all employees share its secret
Allow it to modify all database users
questions.explanation: A service identity should have the minimum permissions and usage scope required. Restricting interactive access and managing credentials reduce unnecessary exposure.

questions.prompt: Why should password hashes normally use a unique salt for each password?
choices: To make identical passwords produce different stored results and impede precomputed attacks
To make passwords recoverable as plaintext
To replace the need for a password hashing algorithm
To encrypt every user's network session
questions.explanation: A unique salt prevents equal passwords from sharing the same hash and reduces reuse of precomputed tables. It should be combined with an appropriate slow password hashing scheme.

questions.prompt: A company wants to protect a private key from direct export while allowing approved cryptographic operations. Which technology best fits?
questions.explanation: An HSM protects keys within a controlled cryptographic boundary and performs supported operations. Access controls, configuration, and backup procedures still matter.

questions.prompt: A browser reports that a server certificate has expired. What should an administrator do?
choices: Renew or replace the certificate through the approved process and verify the deployed chain
Tell all users to ignore certificate warnings permanently
Disable time validation on every client
questions.explanation: An expired certificate no longer meets its validity-period check. Correct certificate lifecycle management restores trusted TLS service without weakening clients' validation behavior.

questions.prompt: A vulnerability scanner finds many issues, but one affects an Internet-facing service, is actively exploited, and exposes sensitive data. What should guide prioritization?
choices: Exploit activity, exposure, asset importance, and business impact
Only the age of the scanner's output file
The number of characters in the vulnerability name
questions.explanation: Remediation should be risk-based rather than a simple list order. Active exploitation, reachable attack paths, and sensitive assets can make an issue urgent.

questions.prompt: How does a penetration test differ most directly from a routine vulnerability scan?
choices: It attempts authorized exploitation to validate attack paths and impact
It guarantees that no vulnerability remains afterward
It can always proceed without owner permission
questions.explanation: A penetration test uses an agreed scope and authorization to validate weaknesses through controlled exploitation. Neither testing nor scanning proves that a system has no remaining weaknesses.

questions.prompt: A security team wants to correlate authentication failures from many hosts and alert on suspicious patterns. Which platform is designed for this purpose?
choices: Security information and event management system
questions.explanation: A SIEM collects and correlates security telemetry from multiple sources. Useful alerts depend on data quality, detection rules, tuning, and a response process.

questions.prompt: An endpoint detection system identifies a process encrypting large numbers of files unexpectedly. What is an appropriate initial response under the incident plan?
choices: Isolate the endpoint to limit spread and preserve relevant evidence
Copy the executable onto all shared servers
Reset administrator passwords from the suspected endpoint
questions.explanation: Containment can reduce additional damage while evidence is preserved. Further eradication and recovery should follow the incident plan and verified findings.

questions.prompt: Why should responders record every transfer of a collected evidence drive?
choices: To make the drive writable by everyone
To replace the need for evidence integrity checks
questions.explanation: Chain-of-custody records document who controlled evidence and when. They complement integrity checks and appropriate storage rather than replacing those safeguards.

questions.prompt: An organization can tolerate losing no more than 15 minutes of transaction data after an outage. Which recovery target describes this limit?
questions.explanation: RPO expresses the acceptable amount of data loss in time. RTO expresses the targeted duration for restoring a service after disruption.

questions.prompt: A service must be restored within two hours after a major outage. Which target is being specified?
questions.explanation: RTO is the target time to recover service. It is distinct from RPO, which describes how much recent data loss the business can tolerate.

questions.prompt: Which backup design best reduces the risk that ransomware encrypts both production data and every recovery copy?
choices: Maintain protected offline or immutable backups and regularly test restoration
Keep the only backup permanently writable from production administrator accounts
Store all backups on the infected user's desktop
Disable backup monitoring to avoid alerts
questions.explanation: Protected offline or immutable copies reduce an attacker's ability to alter recovery data. Restore tests establish whether those copies can actually support recovery.

questions.prompt: A company buys cyber insurance to cover part of the financial consequences of a specified incident. Which risk treatment does this represent?
questions.explanation: Insurance transfers defined financial exposure subject to policy terms. The organization retains other risks and still needs preventive and response controls.

questions.prompt: A business impact analysis identifies critical activities and the consequences of their disruption. What is its primary use?
choices: Inform continuity priorities and recovery requirements
Prove that every threat has been removed
Guarantee that insurance claims will be paid
questions.explanation: A BIA helps determine which services matter most and how disruption affects operations. These findings support recovery priorities and continuity planning.

questions.prompt: A supplier will process sensitive customer data. What should the customer assess before granting access?
choices: The supplier's relevant security controls, contractual obligations, and ongoing oversight arrangements
Whether every employee uses the same desktop wallpaper
Only the number of pages on the supplier's website
questions.explanation: Third-party risk review considers how the supplier protects the data and meets agreed obligations. Oversight must continue as the relationship and risks change.

questions.prompt: A dataset replaces names with codes, but a separate lookup table can reconnect each code to a person. What is this technique?
questions.explanation: Pseudonymized data can be relinked using additional information. It should not be treated as irreversibly anonymous simply because direct names were removed.

questions.prompt: An audit finds that terminated employees retain active accounts. Which process should be improved most directly?
questions.explanation: Offboarding should remove unneeded access promptly and address active sessions and credentials as required. Periodic access reviews help detect accounts missed by the process.

questions.prompt: A BC food handler checks a refrigerator holding potentially hazardous food. Which temperature meets the usual cold-holding limit?
choices: Room temperature if the door stays closed
questions.explanation: BC food-safety guidance uses 4 degrees C or colder for cold holding of potentially hazardous food. Measure actual food and equipment temperatures and act on unsafe readings.

questions.prompt: What is the usual minimum hot-holding temperature for potentially hazardous food in BC?
questions.explanation: Hot-held potentially hazardous food should be maintained at 60 degrees C or hotter. Holding equipment maintains safe temperatures and should not be relied on to reheat cold food rapidly.

questions.prompt: Which cooling schedule follows the standard BC two-stage method for cooked potentially hazardous food?
choices: 60 to 20 degrees C within 2 hours, then 20 to 4 degrees C within 4 more hours
60 to 20 degrees C within 4 hours, then 20 to 4 degrees C within 8 more hours
Leave at room temperature overnight, then refrigerate
Cool from 60 to 4 degrees C at any rate over 24 hours
questions.explanation: The two stages limit time in temperatures that support microbial growth. Both stages must be met; a six-hour total does not authorize taking more than two hours for the first stage.

questions.prompt: A large pot of cooked soup must be cooled safely. Which method is most appropriate?
choices: Divide it into shallow containers and use an approved rapid-cooling method while monitoring temperatures
Leave the covered pot on the counter overnight
Add more hot soup whenever the surface cools
Put the deep covered pot in a crowded refrigerator without checking cooling times
questions.explanation: Smaller, shallower portions and methods such as an ice-water bath help heat escape. Verify the required cooling stages rather than assuming placement in a refrigerator is enough.

questions.prompt: Which temperature range is commonly called the food danger zone in BC food-safety training?
questions.explanation: Many foodborne microorganisms can multiply when potentially hazardous food remains between 4 and 60 degrees C. Limit time in this range through proper preparation, cooling, and holding.

questions.prompt: A cook needs to verify that the centre of a poultry portion has reached its required cooking temperature. What is the best method?
choices: Use a clean, sanitized, suitable food thermometer in the thickest part, avoiding bone
Check only whether the outside is brown
Ask whether the oven feels hot
Taste a small piece before the cooking time ends
questions.explanation: Colour and cooking time alone are unreliable measures of internal temperature. Correct thermometer placement and a suitable probe provide a direct measurement at the relevant location.

questions.prompt: Which internal temperature is generally required for cooking individual chicken pieces in BC guidance?
questions.explanation: Chicken pieces should reach an internal temperature of 74 degrees C. Whole poultry has a different recommended endpoint, so do not assume the pieces' temperature applies to every poultry preparation.

questions.prompt: A worker measures cooked rice at 45 degrees C in a hot-holding unit and cannot establish how long it has been below the required temperature. What is the safest action?
choices: Set it aside from service and follow the food-safety plan's discard and corrective-action procedure
Serve it quickly without recording the problem
Mix it into a fresh batch of hot rice
Assume it is safe because it smells normal
questions.explanation: An unknown time at an unsafe holding temperature cannot establish safe service. Follow the documented plan and supervisor direction; smell and mixing do not make unsafe food safe.

questions.prompt: How should a worker wash hands before preparing ready-to-eat food?
